text:
morgan: FYI hit a reproducible p99 spike during a burst yesterday when autoscaler added capacity. p50/p95 unchanged, but tail shot up to ~1.6s for ~30s window. attaching brief trace snippet

raj: ugh. same pattern as the last cold-handshake case? rough numbers?

morgan: p50 ~75ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~1600ms. scale-up lag ~12s from prober signal to pods ready, then another ~6s of kernel fallback thrash. logs: `kernel_select: chosen=fastpath_fp16 seq_dist=short->long mismatch kv_hit=0`

alyssa: can you paste the exact log lines? need to see kernel variant and batch size at the time.

morgan: snippet:
```
2026-03-17T08:42:17Z node-32 kernel_select: variant=fused_attn_avx2 batch=8 seq=256 -> selected=fused_fp16 fallback=nnpack
2026-03-17T08:42:18Z runtime: kv_cache: miss rate=0.82 priming_in_progress=true
2026-03-17T08:42:29Z rts: handshake: cold_kv_load=420ms kernel_switch=960ms total=1620ms req_id=abc123
```

chee: that `seq=256 -> selected=fused_fp16` looks suspicious — the prober probably sampled short sequences but the burst had longer context. kernel selector picked optimized kernel for short sequences, then when longer ones came it fell back and JIT/rehydrated paths were slow.

raj: also kv cache miss rate 82% while priming_in_progress=true. autoscaler brought new nodes but we didn't prime their KV stores before sending traffic. combined with kernel mismatch that explains the tail.

alyssa: two levers: (1) prewarm KV on scale-up (small prefix replay), (2) make kernel selector conservative during scale events (prefer stability over highest perf).

morgan: agreed. quick mitigation proposal: on prober->scale event set microbatch target from 8 -> 4 and force kernel_selector.bias_towards_stable=true for 30s. prime KV by replaying top-100 prefixes at pod readiness.

raj: sounds good. microbatch downshift reduces queueing + avoids batching into wrong kernel path. do we have telemetry to flip that flag for just the new pool?

alyssa: yes, runtime supports per-pool override. infra-bot: rolling config change applied to pool=burst-pool: {microbatch_override:4, kernel_bias:stable, kv_preload:true} by morgan

morgan: I'll run a canary tonight on testbed and capture p99 before/after. can someone remind me the prober sampling rate?

chee: prober samples 0.5% by default, 2% in high-traffic tiers. increase to 5% temporarily for faster kernel profile convergence.

raj: long term we should add a small prewarm lifecycle hook: when a node joins mark it as warming and route a steady 1 QPS of synthetic prefixes to fully populate KV and kernel warm caches before live traffic routing.

alyssa: Agreed. add experiment: `prewarm-hook=true, prober-rate=5%, microbatch-drift=auto` and measure cost vs p99 improvement. we should log cost delta in console.

morgan: actionable items I took: 1) canary config applied to burst-pool 2) schedule canary @23:00 PST 3) perf traces collection enabled (perf + flamegraphs) 4) create a small eval harness to replay prefixes for prewarm.

raj: I'll help analyze traces once canary runs. if p99 reduces to <350ms we're good to roll.

infra-bot: canary scheduled by morgan for 2026-03-17T23:00:00Z on testbed-burst-pool. logs will be in /infra/canaries/2315009876

morgan: thanks. quick note — if anyone sees autoscaler prober floods during office hours, we probably increased prober rate; revert if it causes noise. :ear:
